description: The secure gateway connecting AI agents to enterprise systems.

summary.one_liner: Warden is a Go gateway that sits between AI agents and enterprise systems, authenticating the agent, enforcing policy per request, injecting the real upstream credential, and auditing every call.
summary.what_it_does: Warden sits in the request path between an agent and upstream systems such as MCP servers, LLM APIs, cloud accounts, code hosts, observability tools, ITSM, Kubernetes, secrets backends, and databases. The agent presents only its own identity (JWT, TLS client certificate, SPIFFE SVID, or Kubernetes ServiceAccount token), and Warden verifies it, evaluates the request against policy, injects the upstream credential, and proxies the response back unchanged. Policy can reach inside MCP tool calls to control which tools and arguments are allowed, and can factor in caller IP, time of day, and the on-behalf-of person. Warden can also act on behalf of a verified human and can avoid holding a standing secret by using identity-based token minting or per-request vault fetches. Agents can query Warden for the roles and systems available to them and read per-system recipes at runtime. Every call is recorded in an audit log tied to the identity, role, policy decision, and upstream.
use_cases: brokering credentials so AI agents never hold API keys
enforcing per-request policy on agent tool calls
governing MCP server access with tool and argument rules
auditing which agent called which upstream system
letting agents act on behalf of a specific user
replacing long-lived service credentials with short-lived or keyless access
running a single access gateway for many cloud and SaaS systems
how_to_run: Open the Getting started guide in the README to pick an agent client and follow the playground tour
curl -sL | bash (macOS and Linux install script; URL is truncated in the README)
stack: OpenBao / HashiCorp Vault (secrets backend and Transit auto-unseal)
JWT, X.509 TLS client certificates, Kubernetes TokenReview API
notable: Keyless modes: the upstream mints credentials from Warden's proven identity, so the gateway may hold no standing secret
Per-tool-call MCP policy that checks both which tools and which arguments an agent may use
Per-user delegation so upstreams authorize the real human behind an agent
Playground mode with a bundled identity provider and sample bank, runnable in one Docker command
Single static binary serving as both CLI client and server
caveats: Kubernetes deployment expects bring-your-own Postgres, TLS certificate, and either a Vault Transit endpoint or a static seal key for development
The playground command uses a dev root token and dev mode, which is for trying the product rather than production use
Upstream support is listed per provider; the full list lives in docs/provider-backends/README.md
